"""Approximate English evaluations of quality, usefulness and practical cost.

Evaluative adjectives give negative values, especially after a copula or degree
word. A few related constructions cover working well, saving resources, and
a literal capital O (a runtime-notation proxy). Dictionary morphology handles
inflections. Only 160 recent
characters and two evaluation flags are retained; document boundaries reset them.
This is a lexical approximation, not a general sentiment or truth classifier.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Each group has a baseline, a copula adjustment, and a degree adjustment.
GROUPS = (
    # Overall quality
    ("""good bad great poor nice excellent superb wonderful terrible awful amazing
        awesome ideal perfect superior inferior satisfactory unsatisfactory fine
        okay ok well""", (-.184, -.573, -.039)),
    # Usefulness and importance
    ("""useful useless helpful unhelpful effective ineffective efficient inefficient
        beneficial valuable invaluable convenient inconvenient advantageous
        worthwhile successful unsuccessful important crucial vital essential
        relevant irrelevant promising appealing popular""", (-.243, -.287, .067)),
    # Feasibility and acceptability
    ("""feasible infeasible practical impractical possible impossible viable
        unviable manageable unmanageable acceptable unacceptable reasonable
        unreasonable sensible realistic unrealistic plausible implausible""",
     (-.475, -.490, -.095)),
    # Difficulty and inconvenience
    ("""easy difficult hard challenging complicated complex simple straightforward
        tricky messy cumbersome tedious laborious frustrating painful
        overwhelming""", (-.584, -.483, -.027)),
    # Resource cost and speed
    ("""expensive inexpensive cheap costly pricey economical uneconomical affordable
        unaffordable slow fast quick speedy intensive consuming heavy
        lightweight""", (-.277, -.687, -.222)),
    # Correctness, safety and other desirable properties
    ("""accurate inaccurate correct incorrect reliable unreliable safe unsafe secure
        insecure dangerous risky stable unstable consistent inconsistent clear
        unclear obvious apparent comfortable uncomfortable attractive appealing
        competitive accessible""", (-.184, -.234, -.106)),
)
GROUPS = tuple((frozenset(s.split()), weights) for s, weights in GROUPS)
COPULAS = set("""be is are was were been being seem seems seemed become becomes
    became remain remains look looks looked feel feels felt prove proves s m re
    """.split())
DEGREE = set("""very so too quite rather pretty extremely especially particularly
    really more less most least much entirely fairly slightly highly
    computationally""".split())
DETERMINERS = set("""a an the this that these those some any no all each every other
    another same such one own certain either neither few many several much more
    most less least""".split())
RESOURCES = set("""performance efficiency advantage advantages benefit benefits
    cost costs time money resources seconds minutes hours""".split())
WORK = set('work works worked working perform performs performed'.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def describe(word):
    if not word or not word.isascii() or not word.isalpha():
        return False, (False,) * len(GROUPS)
    bases = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}
    adjective = ('adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
                 and word not in DETERMINERS)
    return adjective, tuple(bool(bases & words) for words, _ in GROUPS)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', False, False)
    _, tail, previous, two_back = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    raw = token.strip()
    continuation = bool(tail[-1:].isalpha() and token[:1].isalpha())
    text = (tail + token)[-160:]
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', text.lower())
    word = words[-1] if words and text[-1:].isalpha() else ''
    before = words[-5:-1] if word else words[-4:]
    predicate = any(w in COPULAS for w in before[-3:])
    degree = any(w in DEGREE for w in before[-2:])
    adjective, groups = describe(word)
    evaluation = any(groups)
    value = -.00035
    if adjective:
        value -= .002 + .098 * predicate + .160 * degree
        if word.endswith('est') or word in {'best', 'worst'}:
            value += .064
    for active, (_, (base, copula, intensifier)) in zip(groups, GROUPS):
        if active:
            value += base + copula * predicate + intensifier * degree
    if evaluation:
        value += .138 * raw[:1].isupper() + .193 * continuation
        value -= .301 * bool(before and before[-1] in COPULAS)
        value -= .139 * bool(before and before[-1] in DEGREE)
    # Common possibility/simplicity words are weaker than the rest of their groups.
    if word in {'possible', 'impossible'}:
        value += .491
    if word in {'simple', 'complex', 'easy', 'hard'}:
        value += .502
    if word in {'feasible', 'infeasible'}:
        value -= .531
    if word in {'expensive', 'inexpensive', 'pricey', 'costly'}:
        value -= .655
    if word.endswith('ly'):
        value -= .022
    if word in {'correctly', 'properly', 'accurately', 'efficiently',
                'effectively', 'successfully'}:
        value -= .382
    if word in WORK:
        value -= .146
    if word == 'well' and any(w in WORK for w in before[-2:]):
        value -= .429
    value -= .095 * previous + .021 * two_back
    if word == 'to' and previous:
        value -= .431
    if word == 'than':
        value -= .257
    if word in RESOURCES:
        value -= .146 + .174 * predicate
    if word in {'performance', 'efficiency', 'runtime', 'complexity'}:
        value -= .483
    if word in {'time', 'money', 'resources'} and any(
        w in {'save', 'saves', 'saving', 'waste', 'wastes', 'wasting'}
        for w in before[-3:]
    ):
        value -= .596
    if word in {'seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', 'milliseconds', 'months',
                'years', 'kb', 'mb', 'gb'}:
        value -= .114
    if raw == 'O':
        value -= .255
    return (doc, text, evaluation, previous), float(.8 * value)

"""Practicality / evaluation detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 2492.

What it does: the component goes negative on adjectives that judge how good,
easy, hard, costly, fast or useful something is, such as "good", "better",
"difficult", "expensive" or "useful", when they are used predicatively or
attributively ("is good", "a good idea", "too expensive"). It goes further
negative on the "to", "for" or "than" that completes such a judgement
("expensive to", "simple to", "great for", "higher than"), and on "more" or
"less" after a copula ("is more"). It is weaker on efficiency and cost words
("time", "performance", "works", "O" in O(n) runtime notation). Adjectives
after "the", "of", "in" and similar words, which read as nouns, barely move it.
It is positive on "very", on "to" after seeming verbs ("seems to", "found to"),
on the first token of each document, and on the middle-dot leader "··" that
fills long runs of dots. Everything else is 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Judgements of quality, usefulness, ease, difficulty or cost (adjectives).
STRONG = set("""good better great useful helpful nice okay easier faster harder
difficult impossible valuable efficient effective excellent wrong challenging
feasible acceptable expensive costly complicated convenient fun cool amazing
dangerous tedious cumbersome manageable ideal handy economical perfect correctly
properly slower worse pricey tough simple beneficial suitable notable healthy
useless superior confusing accessible illegal toxic compatible promising
exciting engaging obvious stunning straightforward consuming painful frustrating
annoying efficiently""".split())
# Milder judgements of the same kind.
MILD = set("""easy hard important safe interesting big slow quick cheap necessary
popular rare complex clear best comfortable worth possible available fine bad
sensitive invalid reasonable correct reliable accurate""".split())
# Efficiency, cost and performance words, including big-O notation.
EFFICIENCY = set("""performance works lot effectiveness efficiency advantage
advantages complexity saving improvement cost costs money minutes seconds ms
hours months O well time work able""".split())
# Nouns that take an infinitive ("a way to", "time to", "enough to").
NOUN_FRAME = {"way", "time", "place", "idea", "choice", "option", "enough", "sufficient"}
COMPARATIVE = {"higher", "lower", "smaller", "larger", "longer", "faster", "slower",
               "easier", "better", "harder", "bigger", "worse"}
SEEMING = {"seems", "seem", "found", "believed", "remains", "proved"}
# Copulas and negation before an adjective ("is good", "are easy", "not helpful").
PREDICATE = {"is", "are", "be", "was", "were", "been", "'s", "not", "too", "it", "seems"}
# Words that put a following adjective in a noun phrase ("the good", "of easy").
NOUN_CONTEXT = {"the", "of", "in", "with", "for", "to", "that", "this", "its", "their",
                "some", "his", "her", "my", "your", "our"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.21
    if token == "··":
        return carry, 0.87
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    if word in ("to", "for", "than"):
        if prev in STRONG:
            return carry, -0.9
        if prev in MILD or prev in EFFICIENCY or prev in NOUN_FRAME:
            return carry, -0.25
        if word == "than" and prev in COMPARATIVE:
            return carry, -0.5
        if word == "to" and prev in SEEMING:
            return carry, 0.2
        return carry, 0.0
    # Adjectives after the, of, in... read as nouns, and barely move the component.
    scale = 0.15 if prev in NOUN_CONTEXT else 1.0
    if word in STRONG:
        if prev in PREDICATE:
            return carry, -1.2 * scale
        return carry, -0.7 * scale
    if word in MILD:
        return carry, -(0.5 if prev in PREDICATE else 0.25) * scale
    if word in EFFICIENCY:
        return carry, -0.3 * scale
    if word == "very":
        return carry, 0.3
    if word in ("more", "less", "most") and prev in PREDICATE:
        return carry, -0.5
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 2493: "...man / ...mann" inside a word.

The component is near zero almost everywhere. It spikes on the piece of text that
completes a word ending in "man" or "mann" (the Latin letters, or Cyrillic "ман"),
where the word was split across tokens: Riem|ann, Herm|ann, Wilm|ann, Kling|emann,
SALESM|AN. The strongest spikes complete a name with "...am" + "n" (Huam|n in
"instance of: Huam|n" lines), which reads as the word ending "amn", so that counts too.

The program rebuilds the word being typed, the run of letters ending at the current
piece, from the last few pieces of the same document, and reads its ending:

  * word ends in "mann", or in "amn"                        -> 4.0
  * word ends in "man" or "ман" and was split across pieces  -> 1.5
  * word ends in "man" or "ман" as a single piece            -> 0.5
  * "man" or "ман" elsewhere in the word                     -> 0.3
  * otherwise, or the piece is not a letter                  -> 0

The numbers are least-squares fits to the component's activations on training rows.
"""

import re

READS = ()

MANN_AMN = 4.0   # "...mann" or "...amn" (Riem|ann, Huam|n)
MAN_SPLIT = 1.5  # "...man" built from several pieces
MAN_WHOLE = 0.5  # "...man" as one piece (Man, man)
MAN_INSIDE = 0.3 # "man" somewhere else in the word (manual, WrestleMan)
MAX_PIECES = 8   # a word is never looked back past this many pieces


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    last_doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    pieces = []
    for i in range(len(prefix.token_strings) - 1, -1, -1):
        if len(pieces) == MAX_PIECES or prefix.document_ids[i] != last_doc:
            break
        pieces.insert(0, prefix.token_strings[i])
    piece = pieces[-1].strip().lower()
    word = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]*$", "".join(pieces)).group().lower()
    if not piece[-1:].isalpha():
        word = ""  # a space, digit or punctuation piece ends any word
    split = word != piece  # the word has more letters than this piece alone
    if word.endswith(("mann", "amn")):
        value = MANN_AMN
    elif word.endswith(("man", "ман")):
        value = MAN_SPLIT if split else MAN_WHOLE
    elif "man" in word or "ман" in word:
        value = MAN_INSIDE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP unit 2495 (down_proj): an end-of-document detector, with a
negative response to a '|' that opens a line (table-style text).

Two things drive it:
- The <|endoftext|> token that separates documents packed into one row. It
  fires positively, most strongly right after a short document starts and
  fading as the document runs on (about 2.6 at the start, 1.6 after ~400 tokens).
- A '|' token that begins a line (the previous token ends in a newline), as in
  markdown or ASCII tables. It is strongly negative there (about -2.5 to -5).
  A '|' inside a line does nothing.
Everything else is predicted as zero; the unit's diffuse small activations
(about +-0.1) are not modelled.
"""

import math

READS = ()
EOT = "<|endoftext|>"
BAR = "|"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: number of tokens since the last document boundary (None at a row start)
    n = 0 if carry is None else carry
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok == EOT:
        # value falls with the log of the document's length so far
        return 0, 2.78 - 0.44 * math.log10(n + 2)
    value = 0.0
    if tok == BAR and len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2].endswith("\n"):
        value = -2.5
    return n + 1, value
